examples.en: The government collects taxes based on income.
The city hall is collecting parking fees.
The club collected dues every month.
The tax office is in charge of collecting taxes.

examples.ko: 벌금을 징수할 때는 영수증을 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When collecting a fine, you must give a receipt.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 생겨서 요금을 따로 징수하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Under the new system, they decided to charge the fee separately.

explain: '징수하다'는 국가나 단체가 세금, 요금을 걷을 때 써요. 돈을 내는 사람은 '납부하다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 친구들끼리 돈을 모을 때는 '걷다', '모으다'라고 말하고 '징수하다'는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 은행이 돈을 보낼 때 수수료를 징수해요.
phrases.en: The bank collects a fee when you send money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이나 회사가 서비스 값으로 정해진 돈을 걷을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an organization collects a set fee for a service.

phrases.en: This road collects a toll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 지나가는 차에게 요금을 걷을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for collecting tolls from passing cars.

phrases.example: 세금 징수는 매년 같은 달에 해요.
phrases.en: Tax collection happens in the same month every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '징수하다'를 명사로 바꾼 말로, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, often seen in the news.

explain_en: '징수하다' is used when a state or organization collects taxes or fees. The person who pays uses '납부하다', so the two pair up. Friends gathering money say '걷다' or '모으다', never '징수하다'.

examples.en: The thief was arrested last night.
That person was arrested by the police.
They say the arrested man admitted the facts.
If the criminal is arrested, it will be on the news.
He ended up being arrested while running away.
The arrest scene was caught on video.

explain: '잡히다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '체포되다'는 경찰이 법에 따라 잡았을 때 써요. 그래서 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. '경찰에게 체포되다'처럼 '에게'를 써요. 잡은 경찰 쪽 말은 '체포하다'예요.

phrases.en: The arrested person went straight to the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체포를 당한 사람을 가리킬 때 쓰는 꾸밈 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This modifier form refers to a person who has been arrested.

phrases.en: The thief was arrested on the spot in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범죄가 일어난 자리에서 바로 잡혔을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when someone is caught right at the place the crime happened.
phrases.en_equiv: to be arrested on the spot

phrases.en: That person has not been arrested yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 잡히지 않았다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say that someone has not been caught yet.

explain_en: '잡히다' is everyday, while '체포되다' is for when the police catch someone under the law, so you hear it often in the news. It takes '에게', as in '경찰에게 체포되다'. The police side uses '체포하다'.

p.n: 체포당하다 adds a feeling that the arrest was unwanted or unfair.

examples.ko: 정부는 소상공인을 위한 세금 특례를 마련했어요.
examples.en: The government prepared a special tax provision for small business owners.

examples.ko: 이 제도는 일부 지역에만 특례가 적용돼요.
examples.en: A special exception applies only to some regions under this system.

examples.ko: 특례 입학으로 대학에 들어간 학생도 있어요.
examples.en: Some students entered university through special admission.

examples.ko: 시험 특례는 신청서를 내야 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get a special accommodation for the exam only if you submit an application.

examples.ko: 회사가 이번 한 번만 특례로 인정해 줬어요.
examples.en: The company approved it as a special exception just this once.

examples.ko: 특례를 자꾸 만들면 규칙의 의미가 없어져요.
examples.en: If you keep making special exceptions, the rule loses its meaning.

explain: '예외'와 비슷하지만, '특례'는 법이나 제도에서 특별히 따로 정해 둔 규정을 말할 때가 많아요. 그래서 '특례법', '특례 입학'처럼 공적인 말에 잘 나와요. '이번만 봐줄게요' 같은 가벼운 뜻으로는 '예외'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The new special act starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 경우를 따로 정한 법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A law that sets special rules for particular cases.

phrases.example: 외국에서 오래 산 학생은 특례 입학을 신청할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Students who lived abroad long can apply for special admission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 조건을 가진 사람에게 다른 방식으로 입학을 허락하는 제도예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A system admitting people with set conditions by a different path.

phrases.en: A special exception applies in this case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별 규정을 실제로 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually applying the special rule.

explain_en: It is similar to '예외' (exception), but '특례' often refers to a rule specially set apart in a law or system. That is why it appears in official terms like '특례법' and '특례 입학'. For a casual 'I'll let it slide this time', '예외' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Seoul is currently the only special city in Korea.
There are really a lot of people in Seoul Special City.
Citizens directly elect the mayor of a special city.
The address on the envelope starts with Seoul Special City.

examples.ko: 일상에서는 특별시를 빼고 그냥 서울이라고 해요.
examples.en: In daily life we drop the special city part and just say Seoul.
Special cities and metropolitan cities are all big cities.

explain: '서울특별시'가 공식 이름이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '서울'이라고 해요. 부산·대구 같은 큰 도시는 '광역시'예요. 주소를 쓸 때는 '서울특별시 ○○구'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Seoul is a special city and Busan is a metropolitan city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국의 큰 도시 종류를 비교해 말할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together to compare kinds of big cities in Korea.

phrases.en: My address is Mapo-gu, Seoul Special City.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주소를 공식적으로 쓸 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when writing an address formally.

explain_en: '서울특별시' is the official name, and in daily life people just say '서울'. Large cities like Busan and Daegu are '광역시' (metropolitan cities). In addresses, write it like '서울특별시 ○○구'.

examples.en: It is open only on certain days.

examples.ko: 이 약은 특정한 병에만 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine works only for a specific illness.

examples.ko: 특정하게 정해진 사람만 이 방에 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only specifically designated people can enter this room.
I do not use only one particular company's products.
It is a letter sent to no particular person.
The police pinned down the culprit and caught him right away.

explain: '특정'은 '어떤 정해진'이라는 느낌으로 명사 앞에 많이 붙어요. 보통 '특정한 사람', '특정 회사'처럼 말해요. 동사 '특정하다'는 범인을 특정하다처럼 수사 뉴스에서도 들려요.

phrases.en: I only use products from one particular company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특정' 뒤에 명사를 바로 붙이면 '어떤 정해진'이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: '특정' directly before a noun means 'a certain, specific'.

phrases.example: 이 방은 특정한 사람만 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only certain people can use this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특정한'은 '특정'보다 조금 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '특정한' sounds a little softer than plain '특정'.

phrases.en: The police identified the culprit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 여러 가능성 중에서 하나를 정확히 정한다는 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb it means to pin down one among many; common in news.

explain_en: '특정' mostly attaches to a noun to mean a fixed, particular one, as in '특정한 사람' or '특정 회사'. The verb '특정하다' also appears in crime news, for example pinning down a suspect.

en: to correspond to; to be equivalent to; to be tantamount to

examples.en: This rule applies to every student.
It doesn't apply in my case.
Please mark the box that applies.
Children are eligible for this discount.
Only those it applies to should submit the form.

examples.ko: 이 조건에 해당될 때 연락 주세요.
examples.en: Please contact me if you meet this condition.

explain: 조건이나 규칙에 맞아서 적용된다는 뜻이에요. 서류에서 '해당 사항 없음'처럼 자주 보여요. '해당되는 것에 표시하세요'처럼 쓰고, 어떤 사람에게 적용되는지는 '에게'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Mark the place that applies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 설문에서 자주 보이는 꾸밈 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form often seen on forms and surveys.

phrases.en: It doesn't apply to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나와 상관없는 조건일 때 쓰는 고정된 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for a condition that doesn't concern you.

phrases.en: This age falls under the teenager category.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 범위나 종류에 속한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something falls within a certain range or category.

explain_en: It means a condition or rule fits a case and so applies. It appears often on forms in the phrase '해당 사항 없음' (not applicable). The person it applies to is marked with '에게'.

dis.h: apply to; passive form, used as predicate

p.n: Nearly identical; 해당하다 is also common as a modifier like 'the relevant'.

examples.en: Where to bury the nuclear waste is a big problem.
The news covered whether nuclear waste is stored safely.

examples.ko: 핵폐기물 처리 방법을 두고 의견이 갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions are split over how to handle nuclear waste.
I read an article about a nuclear waste storage site.
Nuclear waste can stay dangerous for a long time.
We had a discussion about nuclear waste in class.

explain: 뉴스나 사회·과학 수업에서 보는 말이에요. '처리하다', '보관하다', '매립하다' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요. '핵폐기물 처리장'처럼 뒤에 장소를 나타내는 말을 붙이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a nuclear waste disposal site is being built in our town.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처리장'을 붙여 핵폐기물을 처리하는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 처리장 names the place where it is processed.

phrases.en: Nuclear waste must be stored safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 안전한 보관 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when talking about safe storage.

phrases.en: There is a method of burying nuclear waste underground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에 묻어서 처리한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means disposing of it by burying it in the ground.

explain_en: This word appears in the news and in social studies or science classes. It often goes with verbs like '처리하다' (to process), '보관하다' (to store) and '매립하다' (to bury). A place word can follow it, as in '핵폐기물 처리장'.

en: to be exercised; to be used

examples.en: For a right to be exercised, certain conditions are needed.
The people's rights are being exercised properly.
The day the right to vote is exercised is coming.

examples.ko: 그 힘은 함부로 행사되면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That power must not be exercised carelessly.
The influence that was exerted was too big.
The authority couldn't be exercised, so the work was delayed.

explain: 주로 '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'처럼 법이나 제도 이야기에서만 써요. 소리가 같은 '행사(event)'와 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 능동형 '행사하다'(권리를 행사하다)가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: The police's authority is exercised according to the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리나 권한처럼 공식적인 힘이 쓰일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an official right or authority is put into effect.

phrases.en: The chairperson's influence was strongly exercised at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 힘이 결정에 작용했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that someone's influence had an effect on a decision.

phrases.en: That right has not yet been exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리를 쓰지 못한 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a right could not be used.

explain_en: Mostly used in law and institutions: '권리·권한·영향력이 행사되다'. It is different from '행사' (event). Rare in daily talk; the active '행사하다' (exercise a right) is more common.

examples.en: Under current law, it is hard to punish this behavior.

examples.ko: 현행법에 따르면 만 18세부터 투표할 수 있어요.
examples.en: According to current law, you can vote from age 18.

examples.ko: 현행법이 시대에 맞지 않는다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the current law doesn't fit the times.
The lawyer explained the current law in detail.
Under the current law, this kind of advertising is not allowed.

examples.ko: 현행법과 새 법안의 차이를 정리해 봤어요.
examples.en: I summarized the differences between the current law and the new bill.

explain: 지금 효력이 있는 법을 말해서 '개정안, 법안'과 비교할 때 자주 나와요. '현행법상 ~'은 뉴스와 법률 상담에서 흔한 표현이에요. 이미 없어진 법이나 앞으로 만들 법에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Under current law, this kind of act is illegal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법률 상담에서 지금 법을 기준으로 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news and legal advice when speaking based on the law as it stands.

phrases.en: The National Assembly decided to amend the current law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 있는 법을 고쳐서 바꾼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means changing a law that already exists.

phrases.en: That contract goes against the current law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 어기고 있다는 사실을 조금 격식 있게 지적할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out, somewhat formally, that something violates the law.

explain_en: It refers to a law that is in effect now, so it often appears when compared with an amendment or a bill. '현행법상 ~' is a common phrase in news and legal consultations. It is not used for repealed laws or laws yet to be made.
